fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Open Lawn Area; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Limited Visibility; Detached Structure Complexity
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responders can distinguish it from the road in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so responders can reach the main residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clear passage for emergency vehicles.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot.
• Post the detached structure address or identifier at the vehicle parking area so responders can orient quickly on arrival.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear enough to allow emergency vehicles to turn around, since there is only one way in and out.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Large Trees; Large Trees; Large Trees; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Open Terrain; Woody Debris
wildfire.recommendations:
• Clear woody debris from the ground around the base of the house and any outbuildings.
• Trim tree branches that extend directly over or touch the roof or walls of the house.
• Thin trees on the sides of the house where they are closest to the structure to open up space between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants that are directly against the foundation or walls of the house.
• Separate ground-level vegetation from the base of large trees near the house so fire cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Keep the single driveway clear of overhanging branches to allow emergency vehicles to pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency responders approaching under smoke or low-visibility conditions.
• Keep a turnaround area at or near the house clear so emergency vehicles can reverse direction without backing long distances down the single access route.
